title: Epigenetic profiling of circulating cell-free DNA for early detection and minimal residual disease assessment in lung cancer: a focus on DNA methylation.
authors: Bazan Russo, Tancredi Didier; Gristina, Valerio; Delcuratolo, Marco Donatello; Tamburi, Leonardo; Delli Muti, Francesco; Mangiacotti, Filomena; Mujacic, Clarissa; Fanale, Daniele; Galvano, Antonio; Gori, Stefania; Incorvaia, Lorena; Giordano, Antonio; Pepe, Francesco; Malapelle, Umberto; Russo, Antonio; Muscarella, Lucia Anna; Fabrizio, Federico Pio
one_liner_zh: 该文综述循环游离DNA甲基化表观遗传谱在肺癌早筛和微小残留病监测中的应用，虽涉及染色质组织与机器学习，但核心是临床液体活检生物标志物，缺乏三维基因组/染色质空间架构建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Lung Cancer (LC) continues to be the biggest cause of cancer-related deaths around the world, mostly because of delayed diagnosis. Even if tissue biopsies and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) tests have revolutionized clinical management of LC patients, their effectiveness is restricted in settings with lower tumor burden, molecular heterogeneity, and bias in sampling approaches. In this scenario, the epigenetic profiling of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) stands out as a promising, less invasive approach, accurately detect cancer traces. Evidence from stage I-II disease and CT-detected pulmonary nodules supports the diagnostic potential of cfDNA methylation, although further validation in prospective screening cohorts remains necessary. Beyond genomic alterations, cfDNA epigenetic changes, including DNA methylation, chromatin organization, nucleosome positioning, and fragmentation patterns, reflect multi-dimensional complexity of tumor biology. These properties convey both the functional status and the origin of the circulating DNA fragments, accelerating for tumor integrating genomic analysis. Within this group, DNA methylation is the biologically robust and clinically well-established epigenetic marker, as alterations in methylation linked to cancer often occur in the early stages of tumorigenesis and are commonly found across different cancer cell types. Here, we explored the biological and clinical relevance of the epigenetic landscape of cfDNA in LC patients, particularly focusing on DNA methylation-based biomarkers and their evolving applications towards early diagnosis and post-surgical monitoring of minimal residual disease (MRD). We aimed to comprehensively overview analytical approaches for cfDNA methylation analysis, including targeted and genome-wide profiling strategies, and discuss their integration with machine learning (ML) and multi-omics frameworks in order to improve diagnostic performance and clinical applicability in LC management.
abstract_zh: 肺癌（LC）仍然是全球癌症相关死亡的主要原因，这主要归因于诊断延迟。尽管组织活检和循环肿瘤DNA（ctDNA）检测已彻底改变了肺癌患者的临床管理，但在肿瘤负荷较低、分子异质性和采样方法存在偏差的情况下，其有效性受到限制。在此背景下，无细胞DNA（cfDNA）的表观遗传学分析作为一种有前景且侵入性较低的方法脱颖而出，能够准确检测癌症痕迹。来自I-II期疾病和CT检测到的肺结节证据支持cfDNA甲基化的诊断潜力，尽管在前瞻性筛查队列中的进一步验证仍属必要。除基因组改变外，cfDNA的表观遗传变化，包括DNA甲基化、染色质组织、核小体定位和片段化模式，反映了肿瘤生物学的多维复杂性。这些特性既传达了循环DNA片段的功能状态，也揭示了其来源，促进了肿瘤整合基因组分析。在这一类别中，DNA甲基化是生物学上稳健且临床上已确立的表观遗传标志物，因为与癌症相关的甲基化改变通常发生在肿瘤发生的早期阶段，并在不同癌细胞类型中普遍存在。在此，我们探讨了肺癌患者cfDNA表观遗传景观的生物学和临床相关性，特别关注基于DNA甲基化的生物标志物及其在早期诊断和术后微小残留病（MRD）监测中的不断发展的应用。我们旨在全面概述cfDNA甲基化分析的分析方法，包括靶向和全基因组分析策略，并讨论其与机器学习（ML）和多组学框架的整合，以提高肺癌管理中的诊断性能和临床适用性。
